# Mutations applied to the shipped sources, each rebuilt (SPIR-V and MSL regenerated by
# shaders/regenerate.py for a shader mutation), run on the case it targets, and restored with
# `git checkout`; the tree was clean after every one. Driver: apply -> regenerate -> cmake --build
# build/dev --target <suite> -j4 -> run the suite binary with --test-case=<case> -> restore.
# Host: Linux Mint 22.1, NVIDIA RTX 5060 (Vulkan 1.4), GCC 13, Development build.
#
# Every mutation below turned its case RED. Two earlier attempts are recorded at the end because
# they changed what the suite asserts.

== M1: locate a position by truncating rather than flooring
   src/gameplay/fog/src/fog_of_war.cpp
   case: fog: a position left of the origin is located by flooring, not truncating

== M21: the renderer draws the camp where it stands whatever blue sees
   samples/13-rts-api/host/render.cpp

   RED exit=1 samples/13-rts-api/tests/test_rts_api_fog.cpp:129: ERROR: CHECK_EQ( word_after(fogged.draw, "still0="), std::string("1/1/1") ) is NOT correct!

== Found by mutation, and repaired in the suite
   M1 (locate by truncating) first SURVIVED: every off-origin position the case located was a whole
   number of metres from the origin, where truncation and flooring agree. The case now locates a
   position half a metre left of the origin, which a truncating grid puts in the first column;
   with that assertion the mutation is RED (above).
   M11 (drop the dispatch's early-out for a fully visible pixel) SURVIVED: at t = 1 the lerp
   writes the colour it read to within an f32 ulp, which the rgba16f target rounds away, so the
   branch is not observable and is kept as the statement of the rule rather than as its only
   enforcement. M11b, which shades a visible pixel by 0.995 of its colour, proves case (f) can fail.
